section0.p0: In order to raise the awareness of Vietnam local community in coastal cities and support adopting eco-friendly lifestyles, we run the "Green Ocean" campaign in Nam Dinh (Vietnam) with several activities aiming at secondary school students, resident group leaders and young emerging leaders. Our vision is that marine litter issues in coastal cities will be minimized, when trash will be collected and sent to proper recycling places.

section1.heading: Project objectives
section1.p0: Raise public awareness and encourage local people of all age groups to take practical and positive actions towards zero-waste lifestyles and limit waste amount into the environment
section1.p1: Enhance students' creation, interest and promote STEM initiatives in environmental protection
section1.p2: Provide opportunities for volunteers to "Experience the environment – Aware the current state of the environment – Change the behaviors and take action"
section1.p3: Encourage and empower young people to take action to protect the environment
section1.p4: Reduce the amount of waste released into the sea
section1.p5: One team of young emerging leaders will be provided with a small fund, cleanup tools, and long-term consultancy from Let's Do It! Hanoi to maintain the project
section1.p6: Make cleanup a Culture, not just a Movement!

section2.heading: Background
section2.p0: Increasing marine waste issues have been among the hottest problems in Vietnam. However, these issues in coastal areas have not been paid enough attention. Nam Dinh is a typical coastal province facing these issues, especially in seaside areas because of the flow of major rivers and because people usually throw trash directly into the sea.

col0.heading: Main activities
col0.p0: 02 Environmental Education Programs in 02 secondary schools with 2 activities including 01 training session and 01 recycling STEM festival
col0.p1: 02 Workshops of eco-friendly lifestyles for residential group leaders
col0.p2: 01 cleanup activities for volunteers at 01 beach
col0.p3: 01 online capacity-building workshop for young emerging leaders aged 15-22 (Nam Dinh Youth4Environment Program)

col1.heading: Direct target audience (2,380 people)
col1.p4: Indirect target audience and Demographic: local residents in 2 coastal districts (451,776 people)

section7.heading: Challenge
section7.p0: Covid has been our biggest challenge so far. During the Covid-19 outbreak in Vietnam from August 2021 to March 2022, all activities in Vietnam were restricted. It was very hard to work with local authorities or partners in Vietnam, as our activities can only be organized with the most effective results when held offline. Therefore, we had to wait until the Covid-19 situation was under control so that we could continue our activities.
